tldr: Zebra reported Q4 sales of $1,475M (+10.6% reported, +2.5% organic) and non-GAAP EPS of $4.33 (+8.3%), with adjusted EBITDA margin flat at 22.1% despite service/software pressure and $76M of restructuring charges. FY2026 guidance calls for 9% to 13% sales growth, non-GAAP EPS of $17.70 to $18.30, and at least $900M of free cash flow, with management planning to fully offset an estimated 2-point memory cost headwind.
bullets: Q4 results came in above outlook: net sales were $1,475M, adjusted EBITDA was $326M (22.1% margin), and non-GAAP EPS was $4.33.

Growth was broad but uneven: Connected Frontline organic sales rose 3.6% and Asset Visibility & Automation rose 1.3%; Asia Pacific (+13%), Latin America (+8%), and EMEA (+4%) offset a North America decline (-1%) against tough large-order comps.

2026 setup points to continued growth with execution risk: management guided Q1 sales growth of 11% to 15% and FY2026 sales growth of 9% to 13%, while using pricing, sourcing, and productivity actions to offset memory inflation starting in Q2.
themes: Asset visibility and data capture adoption expanding
Industrial and logistics demand uneven by region
Portfolio shifts and M&A reshaping focus
Pricing and cost pressure shaping margins

segments.title: Core performance and mix
points: Q4 net sales were $1,475M (+10.6% reported, +2.5% organic), with Connected Frontline sales of $854M and Asset Visibility & Automation sales of $621M.
Connected Frontline organic growth was +3.6% (led by mobile computing), while Asset Visibility & Automation organic growth was +1.3% (led by printing and supplies).
Vertical commentary highlighted relative strength in healthcare, manufacturing, and retail/e-commerce, while transportation and logistics cycled tougher prior-year compares in North America.

segments.title: Regional demand and pipeline
points: Regional organic growth was Asia Pacific +13%, Latin America +8%, EMEA +4%, and North America -1%.
Management described run-rate North America demand as solid, with weaker year-over-year comparison tied to fewer very large project orders versus last year.
EMEA returned to growth with strength in Northern and Central Europe; Japan, India, Brazil, and Mexico were called out as bright spots.

segments.title: Margin structure and mitigation plans
points: Adjusted gross margin declined 50 bps to 48.2%, primarily due to lower services and software margins (including higher repair costs in services).
Adjusted operating expense leverage improved 60 bps, supporting a flat 22.1% adjusted EBITDA margin and non-GAAP EPS growth of 8.3%.

Management said existing tariff impacts were fully mitigated and guided to fully offset an estimated 2-point gross margin headwind from memory inflation beginning in Q2 via pricing, sourcing, product actions, and productivity savings.

segments.title: Portfolio actions and capital allocation
points: Zebra continued integrating Elo Touch and Photoneo, while exiting the robotics business to reallocate toward RFID, machine vision, and AI-powered solutions.
FY2025 free cash flow was $831M (102% conversion), with year-end cash of $125M, debt of $2.511B, and net leverage around 2.0x.
The company repurchased $587M of shares in FY2025 and received an additional $1B authorization, with management indicating an aggressive buyback posture into 1H26.

guidance.note: includes ~7 points from acquisitions and FX

notes.title: AI and solution positioning
points: Management framed AI as a multi-year growth driver, with asset visibility data feeding models and connected frontline devices/software delivering model outputs to workers.
Frontline AI Suite includes enablers, blueprints, and Zebra Companion agents; paid pilots are underway with scaled deployments expected in 2026.

notes.title: Refresh and pipeline cadence
points: Retail refreshes were described as more normalized and spread over longer horizons, while large transportation/logistics refreshes tend to run on slower 4-5 year cycles.
Management expects similar large-project refresh activity in 2026 versus 2025, with additional multiyear transportation/logistics deployments more likely to begin in 2027.

themes.title: Memory inflation and pricing offsets
points: Management said memory pricing creates an estimated 2-point gross margin headwind starting in Q2 on a gross basis.
Offset plan includes March price increases, supplier co-planning and alternative memory sourcing, product redesign, tariff/supply-chain actions, and productivity from the robotics exit.

themes.title: Demand visibility and regional setup
points: Leadership cited healthy backlog and pipeline into 2026, with Q1 guide roughly in line with Q4 partly due to less typical seasonality and Elo mix.
North America softness was framed as mostly cyclical comp pressure in large deals, while EMEA and APAC trends improved.

themes.title: RFID, AI, and refresh cycle trajectory
points: RFID adoption was described as broadening across markets, and management called for high double-digit RFID growth in 2026.
AI-capable device specs (memory/processing) and new features such as embedded RFID are expected to support next-generation refresh decisions.

top_questions.question: How much margin pressure should investors expect from memory cost inflation in 2026?
top_questions.summary: Management quantified an approximate 2-point gross margin headwind beginning in Q2 but said full-year guidance already assumes complete mitigation through pricing, sourcing, and productivity actions.

top_questions.question: Why is Q1 revenue guidance comparatively strong versus typical seasonality?
top_questions.summary: Executives attributed the setup to a strong Q4 finish, less year-end spending surge than usual, healthy backlog/pipeline, and Elo's more linear seasonality profile.

top_questions.question: What are the assumptions for large project demand, refreshes, and RFID growth in 2026?
top_questions.summary: The company expects a similar level of refresh-driven large project activity as 2025, sees larger transportation/logistics multiyear programs skewing to 2027 starts, and guided to high double-digit RFID growth in 2026.

implications: Zebra's AI positioning links physical-world data capture (RFID, machine vision, scanning) with frontline execution, which can increase software and services attach beyond device unit growth.
The Elo integration expands store and self-service touchpoints, creating cross-sell paths across mobility, kiosks, and digital engagement workflows.
If memory inflation is offset as planned, FY2026 could show operating leverage despite continued investment in AI, RFID, and machine vision.
competitive_notes: Pricing actions on memory and tariffs appear industry-wide, but Zebra emphasized differentiated value (AI-ready specs, embedded RFID, workflow software) to sustain pricing.
Robotics exit narrows focus to higher-conviction automation areas where management sees stronger returns and clearer product-market fit.
forecast_hooks: Track Q2 gross margin progression as memory costs flow through and March pricing actions annualize.
Monitor conversion from paid AI pilots to scaled production deployments and software revenue contribution in 2026.
Watch machine vision return-to-growth trajectory and RFID momentum outside core retail/logistics use cases.

action_items: Validate March pricing realization and supplier availability assumptions against channel checks heading into Q2.
Track Elo and Photoneo integration milestones, especially cross-sell wins tied to modern store and automation workflows.
Monitor services repair-cost trends to confirm management's expectation for flatter services/software margin through 2026.
open_questions: How quickly will Frontline AI Suite pilots convert into recurring, material software revenue?
Can Zebra sustain current pricing power if memory/tariff dynamics normalize faster than expected?
Will transportation and logistics refresh timing move forward from 2027 if customer visibility improves in 2026?
watch_next_quarter: Q1 growth quality: organic versus acquisition/FX contribution and regional mix.
Gross margin bridge detail: memory headwind realized versus mitigation achieved.
Share repurchase pace relative to free cash flow generation and leverage targets.
